entries.name: verifier-call-deleted-registration-intact
entries.claim: THE SURVIVOR THE REVIEW NAMED, and the first mutation run. Delete one verifier CALL from #post and leave its registration intact: construction still proves a read-back is registered for the effect-reservation companion, and assertObservedWriteSetIsDerived still finds the written relation derived, so before this packet the posting committed with the reservation never observed. The reservation IS written (by the trigger the compiled target declares), so the executed-verifier comparison finds a written relation with no token and refuses before commit, naming the relation. This is the subject-absent vector for R3, held on the exact registration whose verifier the writer inventory already pins.

entries.name: verifier-returns-without-observing
entries.claim: A VERIFIER THAT RETURNS WITHOUT OBSERVING ITS RELATION. The call is present and the registration is intact; the posted-stock balance verifier simply returns before reading a row, which is what a call-site-only mechanism would count as executed. A token is minted from a row PostgreSQL returned, never from the function having been entered, so no token exists for the balance relation the trigger wrote and the posting refuses naming it. Distinct from the deleted-call entry by relation: this red names the balance table, that one names the reservation table.

entries.name: coverage-read-from-the-registry-not-the-tokens
entries.claim: A PROXY SATISFIED WHILE THE FACT DOES NOT HOLD. The comparison keeps running but reads coverage off the construction-time REGISTRY restricted to the written relations -- a relation counts as verified because a read-back is registered for it -- which is exactly the pre-packet state this row was opened against. Both directions of the set comparison are then trivially equal and the unverified-path control commits.

entries.name: token-minted-for-an-unwritten-relation
entries.claim: THE SECOND DIRECTION. A token is a claim about this transaction's writes, and the comparison is an EQUALITY, so a verifier claiming a relation the posting did not write is refused rather than read as extra coverage. The movement read-back is registered for the partitioned PARENT as well as its partitions, and PostgreSQL counts a routed insert on the leaf only (measured), so minting the parent from the registration -- a relation the verifier is registered for but no row came back from -- is a token for an unwritten relation. Without this direction a verifier could cover a relation by naming it.

entries.name: token-minted-by-an-unregistered-verifier
entries.claim: COVERAGE MAY ONLY BE CLAIMED BY THE READ-BACK CONSTRUCTION PROVED FOR THE RELATION. The reservation rows are minted under the movement read-back's name, so the reservation relation carries a token from a verifier the registry does not bind to it. The ledger is checked against the same registry construction proved complete, and a token from the wrong verifier refuses; otherwise any verifier that happened to read a relation could stand in for the one that compares its columns.

entries.name: version-four-digest-covers-the-derived-role
entries.claim: 5g3-prog R2. Version 4 covers exactly the caller's input. This mutation restores the derived postingRole to the version-4 input -- the one kernel-derived value PUR-2b left in it -- and the stored digest becomes the role twin the test computes independently, which it must not be. The role is a pure function of the covered kind, so ADR-0063's own exclusion argument covers it; the test asserts the twin FIRST so this red is its own rather than the caller's-input red PUR-2b's identities control already owns.

entries.name: active-release-fact-compared-as-a-floor
entries.claim: THE FLOOR RESTORED. hasValidCapabilityFacts accepts any version >= 1, and the round-1 reviewer of PUR-2b warned that a consumer could compare as exact what validation treats as a bound. This mutation makes the provider's own comparison that floor: the fact is read, it is a positive integer, and a release declaring 1 is served by a provider implementing 2. ADR-0063 decision 3 makes the number a major version with no minor axis, so the only correct rule is equality, and this is the proxy-satisfied vector for it.

entries.name: active-release-fact-lookup-finds-nothing
entries.claim: THE CHECK READING ZERO INPUT. The manifest lookup is sent looking for a content hash that cannot exist, keeping the bound parameter referenced, so the fact query returns no row. An observer that finds nothing must refuse rather than pass, and this holds that refusal together with the lookup: an ordinary posting dies for the could-not-be-read reason instead of committing.

entries.name: definition-detached-from-the-contract
entries.claim: THE DEFINITION STOPS READING THE CONTRACT. The module definition spells the posting capability version as a literal again, at the value it carried for three encodings' worth of drift. The posting fixture is compiled from the live definition, so its release declares 1 while the provider -- which imports the contract -- implements 2, and every posting refuses at the active-release check. This is the control that proves ONE authority: with the definition detached, the runtime observes the split on the first posting instead of every gate staying green.
